course_name_original: Principles of structural design for industry
course_name_en: Principles of structural design for industry

learning_outcomes.text: To know the basic theory of solid and structural mechanics
To know and embrace the concepts of stress state, strain state, constitutive relationship
To know the response of elastic, plastic, elasto-plastic and viscoelastic materials
To understand relations governing the internal action and the elastic curve of a beam
To understand the response of elasto-plastic beam elements under tension/compression, bending, shear, and torsion
To understand the response of 2-dimensional structural elements
To be able to apply the basic concepts of solid and structural mechanics
To be able to determine the stress state, starting from the strain state, and viceversa
To be able to interpret simple programs for the determination and drawing of the internal action diagrams and of the elastic curve of a beam
To be able to describe the stress and strain state of an elasto-plastic beam subjected to tension/compression, bending, shear, and torsion
To be able to describe and classify buckling phenomena
To be able to use the acquired knowledge for autonomously studying and deepening of issues related to solid and structural mechanics
To be able to determine the stress state, starting from the strain state, and viceversa, for solids with different material response
To be able to write simple programs for the determination and drawing of the internal action diagrams and of the elastic curve of a beam
To be able to determine and calculate the stress and strain state of an elasto-plastic beam subjected to tension/compression, bending, shear, and torsion
To be able to classify buckling phenomena and evaluate the related critical loads
To be able to use the acquired knowledge for autonomously studying and deepening of issues related to solid and structural mechanics, and for the design of structural elements
To evaluate the applicability of structural models to describe real structures and elements
To evaluate the applicability of the beam theory and of numerical methods
To assess and compare independently the engineering solutions of a problem with limited complexity
To assess and compare independently the engineering solutions of a problem
To analyze a problem related to solid and structural mechanics, choosing autonomously the right approach and the appropriate tools for its solution
To communicate effectively in written and/or oral form in the context of solid and structural mechanics
To know and know how to use the specific scientific / technical terminology of solid and structural mechanics
To know and know how to use the specific scientific / technical terminology of solid and structural mechanics, possibly also in English
To be able to properly use the mathematical language to describe the treated issues
To catalog, schematize and elaborate the acquired knowledge
To correlate the different topics one other and with the basic and related disciplines
To autonomously use and apply the acquired knowledge

syllabus_topics: Constitutive relations
Revision of analysis of Stress and Strain. Mohr’s circles, classification of stress states.
Constitutive models for engineering materials. Linear and non-linear elasticity, elasto-plasticity
Anisotropic materials
Viscoelasticity
Elastoplastic Analysis of beams
Axially Loaded Members. Plastic deformations
Pure Bending. Plastic deformations and residual stress. Plastic hinges. Moment-curvature relationship
Torsion. Plastic deformations and residual stress. Relationship between torque and angle of twist.
Shear
2-dimensional flat elements
Plane structural elements under in-plane loading. Plane stress state, Airy function
Plane structural elements under out-of-plane loading (flexural response). Kirkhhoff-Love plate theories
Tensioned membranes
Stability and buckling
Buckling of compressed elements. Euler’s critical load.
Structures with concentrated elasticity
Flexural and torsional instabilities. Local instabilities.
Development of numerical codes for the determination of the elastic curve
Introduction to matlab
Revision of Calculus of statically indeterminate structures, internal action relationships and diagrams, moment-curvature relationship, governing differential equation for the elastic curve.
Development of numerical codes (in Matlab) for the determination of the internal action diagrams
Development of numerical codes (in Matlab) for the determination of the elastic curve
teaching_methods: Autonomous development and deep study of issues related to solid and structural mechanics and/or design exercises (individual or small groups)
assessment_rules: The evaluation for both written and oral tests is on a 0-30 scale. Students are admitted to the oral exam if at least 18 points are achieved on the written test. The final mark is the average of the written and oral marks. A '30 cum laude' is given to students who achieve the highest score on each item and use precise vocabulary.
bibliography: F. P. Beer, E. R. Johnston, J. T. DeWolf, D. F. Mazurek, "Meccanica dei solidi - Elementi di scienza delle costruzioni", MCGraw-Hill, 4° edizione (in italian, available also in english).
S. H. Crandall, N. C. Dahl, T. J. Lardner, “Introduction to the Mechanics of Solids”, McGraw-Hill, 2° Edizione.
O. Belluzzi, “Scienza delle Costruzioni”, Zanichelli (in italian).
